rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 2 (score 65.2489): sensors at x = -0.024 to 0.024, y = 0.05, kp 7.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4, last_direction. All 180 development trials across iterations 0 to 2 ended off track with no finishes. Max error sits at 0.061 to 0.068 m, just over the 0.06 m limit, while rms error is steady at 0.024 to 0.030 m. Line losses run 1 to 2 per run. Gain changes have moved the score by less than 0.04 points, so the sensor layout is the untested lever.

Accepted from the round-1 critique: (a) the kp cut to 3.0 and the base_speed cut to 1.3 are rejected. Lower kp reduces turn authority at exactly the peaks where the robot leaves the tape, and speed cuts reduce the only route to the 500-point completion term. (b) The critique's point that the change set was confounded is accepted. This revision changes one thing only: sensor geometry. (c) The critique's engagement arithmetic is accepted: a sensor sees tape out to about 0.02 m beyond its own x position, so outer sensors at x = plus or minus 0.06 keep tape in view at offsets near 0.08 m, past the 0.06 m limit. Inner sensors keep the 0.03 m spacing, and the 0.016 m footprints leave gaps of 0.014 m, which is smaller than the 0.025 m tape, so the tape always covers at least one sensor.

Change: sensor x widened from plus or minus 0.024 to 0.06 (positions -0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06 at y = 0.05). Controller, body, wheels and mass are identical to iteration 2, so any change in max_error, line_loss_events or progress is attributable to the sensor layout. I did not change y to 0.07, because that was part of the earlier confounded draft and is not needed for this test.

Hypotheses: line_loss_events fall to 1 or fewer per run; max_error falls below 0.06 m on at least the oval and s-bend; progress rises above 0.27 on the oval. If max_error stays above 0.06 m with fewer losses, the next test is base_speed or kp, not more sensor spread. If steering_oscillation rises by more than 30 percent, the wider spacing has made the signal too coarse, and the next step is to reduce the spread to x = plus or minus 0.045. Completion at base_speed 1.4 is still untested; completion_time is requested so the next race can show whether the robot is slow or stopped.
